provenance.source: PWT 10.01 (productivity) + UN WPP 2024 (total population; 15+ by-age file absent → labour uses total-pop) + ILOSTAT LFPR (participation) + EU KLEMS & INTANProd 2024 release (sector MFP via LP1ConTFP, per-hour LP, labour share) + NGFS Phase 5 REMIND-MAgPIE 3.3-4.8 / Below 2C (PER-CHANNEL emissions intensity = channel CO2 / channel activity)
provenance.licence: see per-entry sources; UN WPP: CC BY 3.0 IGO, PWT 10.01: CC BY 4.0, ILOSTAT: CC BY 4.0, EU KLEMS: CC BY 4.0, NGFS: see NGFS terms
provenance.notes: Per-region and per-sector annual growth trajectories for the Phase 7b.2 structural drivers, EXTRACTED FROM REAL SOURCES by scripts/extract_structural_sources.py and assembled by scripts/build_structural_trajectories.py (both --check-gated in CI). v5 (review-12 2026-10-14): NGFS emissions_intensity is now PER CHANNEL — electricity=CO2|Supply|Electricity/Secondary Energy|Electricity, industry=CO2|Demand|Industry/FE|Industry, process=CO2|Industrial Processes/(Steel+Cement), transport/buildings over their FE, energy_supply=(Energy|Supply−Electricity)/FE, __all__=(Energy+IndProc)/total FE; the concordance BLENDS these per sector (metals=process+industry, coal/oil_gas=energy_supply, agriculture=economy-wide). The CGE-consistent AEEI term FE/output is NOT sourceable per sector from NGFS and is omitted (confidence LOW); a CO2-only CarbonPrice is required (gas-indexed paths = future). A 15+-population driver (working_age_population) carries the labour identity when the WPP by-age file is present (else total-pop fallback). v4 (review-10): CO2/Final-Energy intensity (superseded by per-channel). v3 (review-8): EU KLEMS mfp = LP1ConTFP directly; capital_deepening retired. Rates are decimal fractions per year; wrapper holds the most recent knot piecewise-constant. N/S region + BRD/MIL productivity-sector archetypes + per-channel emissions. Known limits documented in docs/structural-data-pipeline-plan.md. SENSITIVITY: ADVERSE deterministic stress case (review-10 P1#2; per-driver direction review-11 P2#2 2026-09-19) — NOT a statistical bound or probabilistic interval (NGFS scenarios are not forecasts and carry no probabilities). Direction is PER DRIVER: adverse = LOWER growth for productivity/population/participation/sector-productivity, and SLOWER decarbonisation (less-negative) for emissions intensity. EU KLEMS mfp/sector_productivity: per-archetype envelope across trend windows 2017–21 (central) / 2015–19 / 2010–19; these mix windows and are not one coherent calibration. Other drivers: judgmental relative stress (low±50/medium±25/high±10) on the central rate. 'adverse'/'favourable' order the INPUT drivers, NOT any CGE output — for output bounds run all cases and take the realised per-output min/max. Central = trajectories_v1.json.

sources.emissions_intensity:__all__: NGFS Phase 5 scenario explorer: model REMIND-MAgPIE 3.3-4.8, scenario Below 2°C, region World; PER-CHANNEL emissions intensity (review-11 P1), each CO2 over the activity that drives it: electricity = CO2|Supply|Electricity / Secondary Energy|Electricity (generation); industry = CO2|Demand|Industry / FE|Industry (combustion); process = CO2|Industrial Processes / (Production|Steel + |Cement); transport = CO2|Demand|Transportation / FE|Transportation; buildings = CO2|Demand|Res+Comm / FE|Res+Comm; energy_supply = (Energy|Supply − Electricity) / FE; __all__ = (Energy + Industrial Processes) CO2 / total Final Energy. The concordance BLENDS these channels per model sector (metals = process+industry, coal/oil_gas = energy_supply, agriculture = economy-wide) so electricity gets the generation path, not industry combustion. KNOWN GAP: FE/output (autonomous energy efficiency) is NOT sourceable per sector from NGFS (no sector output/VA) and the Leontief CGE does not reproduce it — these are combustion/energy-emissions intensities, NOT full CO2/output (hence LOW confidence). AFOLU excluded; a knot at every positive source year, CAGR to the next, last held flat (electricity truncates at its last positive year ~2080). https://data.ece.iiasa.ac.at/ngfs/
